validity.recommendation: Keep as a distinct transmission row, but obtain an SSGC network map/annual-report page or an OGRA filing to source the exact specs (see the paired spec concern below) — this row cannot be closed out with only the lead found here.
validity.researcher_notes: gem.wiki is 403'd this run so wiki_citations.json is empty for this row (harvest failure, not 'unsourced sheet') and every ref cell for P4019 came back MISSING_REF -- there was nothing already cited to re-verify, so this is fresh research from zero. WebFetch to the row's own gem.wiki page also 403'd (Cloudflare), so no leads could be pulled from it either. Extensive open-web search (English + Urdu) for 'Dadu-Malir-Karachi Gas Pipeline' by that exact name returns almost nothing except gem.wiki itself and AI-search syntheses that clearly reflect the gem.wiki page content without attributing it (one search assistant invented an unsourced 'Indus Right Bank Pipeline System' label that appears on no real page -- flagged as a hallucination artifact, not used or cited). General SSGC transmission-network aggregate stats (1,888 km / 2,942 km / 3,614 km / 4,126-4,143 km high-pressure pipeline depending on source and year) appear across several outlets but never break out this specific segment. However, independent, non-GEM evidence DOES support that a real gas-pipeline route in this exact corridor exists: Osmani & Company (Pvt.) Ltd, a Pakistani engineering/surveying firm, lists on its own project-portfolio page a completed 'Engineering Survey of Gas Pipeline Route... 1:2000 scale topographic survey... Between Dadu & Karchat' for Sui Southern Gas Co Ltd (SSGC) -- Karchat (Jamshoro district) sits on the same Dadu-to-Karachi/Malir transit corridor through the Kirthar range, so this is a plausible independent trace of the same physical line, not a GEM derivative (verified live via url_verifier). Separately, SSGC's own site (Urdu) documents a GPS/GIS re-route survey of the 'Zarghun South-1 to Quetta TBS' pipeline at ~64 km -- functionally the same naming convention as roster row P4022 'Zarghun-Quetta Gas Pipeline' (sheet len=61 km, a close match) -- which independently validates that SSGC really does name and track individual trunk segments this way (field/place -> destination), lending structural credibility to the whole 'X-Malir-Karachi' family in the roster (P4015 Kadanwari-Malir-Karachi, this row, plus P4014 Nawabshah-Karachi, P4020 Bajara-Karachi Loopline). Classification: as a long-haul interprovincial trunk moving gas from the Dadu-area corridor into the Karachi distribution hub, 'transmission' fits and is not a gathering/feeder line. Duplicate check against the full 63-row roster: not a duplicate of P4015 Kadanwari-Malir-Karachi (different origin field/city, both plausibly converging on a shared Malir hub -- Malir is independently referenced elsewhere as an SSGC TBS/terminal location), nor of P4023 Dadu-Sui Gas Pipeline (same 'Dadu' endpoint but the other leg runs to Sui/Balochistan, a different destination entirely -- consistent with Dadu being a junction city with pipe running two different directions). Net: existence is plausible and partially corroborated (1 independent, weak/partial source -- short of the 2-independent-source bar), so this is not flagged as a bare existence hallucination, but it is not closed out to high/medium confidence either.

validity.recommendation: Do not treat Length=250 km / Diameter=20,18 in / Capacity=400 MMcf/d / Owner=SSGC 100% as verified. Source an SSGC annual report, OGRA State of the Industry report, or PPIS/HDIP Pakistan Energy Yearbook table that names this segment specifically (all attempted this run were either 403'd, image-only scans that would not OCR through the available fetch tool, or aggregate network totals with no segment breakdown) before relying on these numbers in any downstream product.
validity.researcher_notes: No independent source -- not even the one partial lead found for existence (Osmani & Company's survey listing) -- states a length, diameter, or capacity figure for this pipeline, so none of Length=250 km, Diameter=20 in/18 in, or Capacity=400 MMcf/d could be corroborated by even a single outside source, let alone the required 2 independent ones. Tried and struck out on: SSGC's own site (no segment-level table found, only aggregate network-length stats that vary 1,888-4,143 km depending on year/source, itself a sign the public aggregate figures aren't tightly controlled); OGRA 'State of the Regulated Petroleum Industry' report (site returned 403); PACRA's Oct-2022 'Pipeline Network Sector Study' (covers only the 4 major OIL pipelines -- KMK/MFM/WOP/Korangi-Port Qasim -- explicitly excludes gas, per its own note 'Gas pipelines are covered in PACRA Gas distribution report'); two World Bank SSGC/SNGPL project-appraisal PDFs (one on-topic for SNGPL only, one an unreadable scanned image). Owner1=Sui Southern Gas Co (SSGC) 100% is directionally consistent with SSGC being the dominant transmission operator across Sindh/Balochistan (independently confirmed) but the specific 100%-ownership claim for this segment specifically was not independently found either. Given the near-requirement for 2+ independent sources on any data point (status/capacity/length/diameter/ownership), these values should be read as unverified pending a primary SSGC/OGRA/HDIP document, not as confirmed.

summary: P4019 (Dadu-Malir-Karachi Gas Pipeline): existence plausible via one independent, partial lead (Osmani & Co. survey of an SSGC gas-pipeline route 'Between Dadu & Karchat', on the same corridor) and via a validated SSGC segment-naming convention elsewhere (Zarghun-Quetta), but not confirmed to the 2-independent-source bar; no duplicate found against the 63-row roster; but Length/Diameter/Capacity/Owner numbers (250 km, 20/18 in, 400 MMcf/d, SSGC 100%) remain wholly unverified by any independent source -- flagged as an open spec concern, no refs staged for those fields.
